# Part 1: The two-by-two (Lecture 9a)

## Reproduce: a SOX-404-style mandate

Firms with public float of at least \$75M ("accelerated filers") must comply from fiscal 2004; smaller firms are
exempt. The outcome is log audit fees. The true effect is $+0.35$ in 2004, decaying to $+0.20$ by 2007. Larger
firms are on a steeper audit-fee trend: `kappa` is the extra growth per year per standard deviation of size.

```{r}
years <- 2000:2007
tau_sox <- c(`2004` = 0.35, `2005` = 0.28, `2006` = 0.22, `2007` = 0.20)
sim_sox <- function(N = 2000, kappa = 0.06, sd_eps = 0.12) {
  lfloat <- rnorm(N, log(75), 1.2)
  size <- (lfloat - mean(lfloat)) / sd(lfloat)
  d <- CJ(firm = 1:N, year = years)
  d[, `:=`(size = size[firm], acc = as.integer(lfloat[firm] >= log(75)))]
  d[, alpha := 11 + 0.5 * size + rnorm(N, 0, 0.4)[firm]]
  gam <- cumsum(c(0, rnorm(length(years) - 1, 0.03, 0.02)))
  d[, post := as.integer(year >= 2004)]
  d[, tau := 0]
  d[acc == 1 & post == 1, tau := tau_sox[as.character(year)]]
  d[, y := alpha + gam[year - 1999] + kappa * size * (year - 2003) + tau + rnorm(.N, 0, sd_eps)]
  d[, D := acc * post]
  d[]
}
sox <- sim_sox()
```

The four routes to the $2\times2$ (fiscal 2003 vs. 2004):

```{r}
two <- sox[year %in% c(2003, 2004)]
cm <- two[, .(y = mean(y)), by = .(acc, year)]
dd_means <- with(cm, (y[acc == 1 & year == 2004] - y[acc == 1 & year == 2003]) -
                     (y[acc == 0 & year == 2004] - y[acc == 0 & year == 2003]))
w <- dcast(two, firm + acc + size ~ year, value.var = "y")
setnames(w, c("2003", "2004"), c("y03", "y04"))
w[, dy := y04 - y03]
fits <- list(
  fd   = feols(dy ~ acc, w, vcov = "hetero"),
  int  = feols(y ~ acc * post, two, vcov = ~firm),
  twfe = feols(y ~ D | firm + year, two, vcov = ~firm))
c(means = dd_means, fd = coef(fits$fd)[["acc"]], int = coef(fits$int)[["acc:post"]], twfe = coef(fits$twfe)[["D"]])
```

They agree, and they all miss the truth of 0.35. Conditioning on size:

```{r}
fit_cond <- feols(dy ~ acc + size, w, vcov = "hetero")
coeftable(fit_cond)["acc", ]
```

And the event study, with and without size-specific year effects:

```{r}
fit_es   <- feols(y ~ i(year, acc, ref = 2003) | firm + year, sox, vcov = ~firm)
fit_es_c <- feols(y ~ i(year, acc, ref = 2003) + i(year, size, ref = 2003) | firm + year, sox, vcov = ~firm)
iplot(list(fit_es, fit_es_c), main = "Accelerated filers vs. exempt firms (black: unconditional; red: + size x year)")
points(2004:2007 + 0.1, tau_sox, pch = 4, cex = 1.5)   # truth
```

## Reproduce: placebo laws (Bertrand, Duflo and Mullainathan 2004)

A state-by-year panel with AR(1) errors. Half the states "pass a law" in a random year between 6 and 15. The law does
nothing. How often does a 5% test reject?

```{r}
bdm_once <- function(S = 50, T = 20, rho = 0.8) {
  e <- matrix(0, S, T); e[, 1] <- rnorm(S, 0, 1 / sqrt(1 - rho^2))
  for (t in 2:T) e[, t] <- rho * e[, t - 1] + rnorm(S)
  d <- data.table(state = rep(1:S, T), t = rep(1:T, each = S), e = as.vector(e))
  start <- rep(Inf, S); tr <- sample(S, S / 2); start[tr] <- sample(6:15, length(tr), replace = TRUE)
  d[, y := rnorm(S)[state] + 0.1 * t + e]
  d[, D := as.integer(t >= start[state])]
  f <- feols(y ~ D | state + t, d)
  sapply(list(iid = "iid", hetero = "hetero", cluster = ~state),
         function(v) unname(pvalue(summary(f, vcov = v))["D"]) < 0.05)
}
rowMeans(replicate(200, bdm_once(S = 50, rho = 0.8)))
```

# Part 2: Staggered adoption (Lecture 9b)

## Reproduce: an algorithm rolled out city by city

300 cities, 20 months, four launch waves (months 6, 9, 12, 15) and a never-treated group, 60 cities each. The
effect ramps in over eight months and is larger for earlier waves.

```{r}
T_ <- 20; waves <- c(6, 9, 12, 15)
sim_rollout <- function(theta = c(`6` = 0.12, `9` = 0.09, `12` = 0.06, `15` = 0.04), ramp = 8, n_per = 60,
                        groups = c(waves, Inf)) {
  G <- rep(groups, each = n_per); N <- length(G)
  d <- CJ(id = 1:N, t = 1:T_)
  d[, g := G[id]]
  d[, alpha := rnorm(N, 0, 0.3)[id]]
  gam <- cumsum(rnorm(T_, 0.01, 0.02))
  d[, e := t - g]
  d[, D := as.integer(t >= g)]
  d[, tau := 0]
  d[D == 1, tau := theta[as.character(g)] * pmin(e + 1, ramp) / ramp]
  d[, y := alpha + gam[t] + tau + rnorm(.N, 0, 0.05)]
  d[, g_sa := ifelse(is.finite(g), g, 10000)]   # sunab's coding for never-treated
  d[]
}
d <- sim_rollout()
att_true <- d[D == 1, mean(tau)]
att_true
```

Static two-way FE, and the weights it puts on each treated city-month (Frisch--Waugh--Lovell):

```{r}
fit_static <- feols(y ~ D | id + t, d, vcov = ~id)
d[, Dt := resid(feols(D ~ 1 | id + t, d))]
d[D == 1, w := Dt / sum(Dt)]
c(twfe = coef(fit_static)[["D"]], truth = att_true,
  share_negative_rows = d[D == 1, mean(w < 0)],
  estimand_from_weights = d[D == 1, sum(w * tau)])
```

## Reproduce: three clean estimators

Sun and Abraham, via `sunab()`:

```{r}
fit_sa <- feols(y ~ sunab(g_sa, t) | id + t, d, vcov = ~id)
summary(fit_sa, agg = "ATT")
iplot(fit_sa, main = "Sun-Abraham event study")
```

Callaway and Sant'Anna by hand: each $\text{ATT}(g,t)$ is a $2\times2$ against a clean comparison group, relative to
month $g-1$; then average with cohort-size weights.

```{r}
cs_att <- function(d, control = "never") {
  wd <- dcast(d, id + g ~ t, value.var = "y"); Y <- as.matrix(wd[, -(1:2)]); G <- wd$g
  out <- list()
  for (g in waves) {
    ig <- which(G == g); b <- g - 1
    for (tt in g:T_) {
      ic <- if (control == "never") which(!is.finite(G)) else which(G > tt & G != g)
      if (length(ic) == 0) next
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.table(g = g, t = tt, n = length(ig),
        att = mean(Y[ig, tt] - Y[ig, b]) - mean(Y[ic, tt] - Y[ic, b]))
    }
  }
  a <- rbindlist(out)
  a[, weighted.mean(att, n)]
}
c(cs_never = cs_att(d, "never"), cs_notyet = cs_att(d, "notyet"))
```

Imputation: fit city and month effects on untreated observations only, predict $Y(0)$ for the treated, average the gaps.

```{r}
f0 <- feols(y ~ 1 | id + t, d[D == 0])
tr <- d[D == 1]
tr[, tauhat := y - predict(f0, newdata = tr)]
c(imputation = tr[, mean(tauhat)], truth = att_true)
```
